title.narrative: PIP_Strengthening Transparency and Accountability for Results (STAR)

description.narrative: Corruption remains a critical barrier to achieving sustainable development and equitable public service delivery in Tajikistan. To address these challenges, this project proposes the introduction of two Korean internationally recognized and contextually adaptable tools that have proven effective in many countries: Assessment of the effectiveness of anticorruption efforts (Integrity Efforts Assessment, (IEA)) and Digital portal for reporting corruption and violations of public interests (Clean Portal) as well as legislative measures on whistleblower protection. These tools will be localized and implemented in partnership with the Agency for State Financial Control and Combating Corruption of the Republic of Tajikistan and relevant national stakeholders.In line with UNDPs strategic emphasis on South-South Cooperation, the project will facilitate the exchange of knowledge and expertise between Tajikistan and neighboring countries, particularly Uzbekistan, and will also draw from the expert knowledge and experiences of Korea’s Anti-Corruption and Civil Rights Commission.The project places gender equality and social inclusion at the center of its approach, recognizing that corruption disproportionately affects women, youth, and marginalized groups, often limiting their access to public services, participation in decision-making, and protection under the law. Given the innovative and technical nature of the initiative, a Project Initiation Plan (PIP) is being used to enable a timely and well-coordinated start-up phase prior to the launch of the full-fledged project, subject to further resource mobilization. The PIP will enable UNDP and the Agency for State Financial Control and Combating Corruption to conduct key activities such as legal and policy development, development of digital platforms, capacity building interventions etc
